source.title: Kimi Linear: An Expressive, Efficient Attention Architecture
source.authors: Yu Zhang; Zongyu Lin; Xingcheng Yao; Jiaxi Hu; Fan-Qing Meng; Chengyin Liu; Xin Men; Songlin Yang; Zhiyuan Li; Wen-Tao Li; Enzhe Lu; Weizhou Liu; Yan-Ru Chen; Wei-Xin Xu; Long Yu; Ye-Jia Wang; Yu Fan; Longguang Zhong; Enming Yuan; De-Hao Zhang; Yi-Zhi Zhang; T. record.tranche_reason: The study fits loss-versus-compute scaling curves on its own language-model runs, using a scaling-law measurement on new model architectures.
record.gate_note: The paper reports two fitted compute–loss curves. It does not report individual run losses or a test of whether fits from smaller runs predict larger runs. Architecture-ratio ablations report perplexities, but do not state that parameter counts are fixed, so they are not cataloged as tests of V4. Downstream benchmark and RL results do not test whether performance is predictable from scale or pretraining loss.
record.test_reason: The scaling section imposes a power-law form on loss versus compute for two architectures. It uses the fits only to derive an efficiency ratio for its own architecture (about 1.16× for Kimi Linear over MLA). No fit quality, residuals or individual run losses are given. The five-model sweep spans roughly one order of magnitude of compute (653M×38.8B to 1.7B×128B tokens), so the study relies on V1 as a tool rather than testing it.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. Under Chinchilla-style compute-optimal training, Kimi Linear reaches about 1.16× the compute efficiency of tuned MLA baselines. The authors expect tuning KDA's hyperparameters to improve its scaling curves further. KDA reused MLA's hyperparameters without retuning.
record.recipe_differences: The paper says it follows Chinchilla scaling-law methodology and fits loss against compute, but tests Moonlight-based MoE models and reports only two fitted curves. Its KDA sweep retains a 3:1 hybrid ratio and otherwise follows the MLA training configuration.
record.method_sensitivity: The authors tuned MLA hyperparameters separately by model size and state that further careful tuning may improve KDA's scaling curves; no measured sensitivity comparison is reported.

fits_no_version.finding: Replacing 3/4 of MLA layers with KDA lowers the fitted loss coefficient (2.2879 vs 2.3092) with a near-identical exponent (−0.0527 vs −0.0536). The authors read this as about 1.16× compute efficiency.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Attention-architecture changes shift the compute–loss curve's offset rather than its exponent.

record.problems: Only fitted equations are reported for the scaling experiments; individual run losses and uncertainty estimates are not stated. The text does not specify whether the plotted loss is held-out or cross-entropy, and the stated model-size and token ranges are limited.
record.rows_left_out: No scaling-fit rows left out. Perplexity results from the architecture ablations were excluded because the paper does not state that parameter counts are fixed, as required by V4.

untested.parts: Whether the power-law form fits (no residuals or fit quality); scaling in parameters or tokens separately; a range of several orders of magnitude; held-out loss definition.
No extrapolation from small-run fits to larger runs (the 48B/3B-active models are not compared to the fits).
The Table 1 ablations vary hybrid ratio and components at equal FLOPs, not depth or width at fixed parameters.
Downstream scores are not related to scale or loss.
The authors only speculate that tuning would improve KDA's curves; nothing is measured.

record.verdict_notes: This is an architecture technical report. Its scaling section is a tool for comparing architectures, so it is reclassified from T1/tests to T4. The reader's supports and limits_scope labels for V1 are removed. The Table 2 configurations are setup values, not results. The exponents are very small (about 0.053) over a narrow compute window, so they say little about V1's form.

versions.untested_parts: Only fitted loss-versus-compute curves are reported. Independent scaling in parameters or tokens, the non-bottleneck conditions, the held-out/cross-entropy specification, and a several-orders-of-magnitude range are not established in the text.
No small-run fit is evaluated against the loss of larger runs.
No fixed-compute sweep comparing parameter/token allocations or fitted allocation exponents is reported.
The architecture-ratio ablations do not state that parameter counts are fixed and do not test depth or width changes.
No power-law scaling test in another modality or training regime is reported.
Downstream scores are reported, but not as a predictable relationship with model scale or pretraining loss.
The paper notes that further hyperparameter tuning may improve KDA's scaling curves, but does not test how fitting choices change exponents or allocation trends, or whether curves bend.

rows.subject: MLA
rows.operation_detail: Fit loss as a function of training compute across a model-size sweep.
rows.measure: Fitted loss-versus-compute power law; loss type and held-out status not stated.
rows.note: The text gives the fitted equation. The listed model sizes and token counts span a limited range, and individual losses are not reported.
rows.check: The power-law form is assumed and fitted, with no goodness-of-fit or per-run losses reported. The compute range is about one decade, so the row cannot show whether loss follows a power law over several orders of magnitude. Better marked cannot_determine than partial.

rows.subject: Kimi Linear
rows.operation_detail: Fit loss as a function of training compute across a model-size sweep.

conditions.value: MLA training configuration used without other modifications

rows.measure: Fitted loss-versus-compute power law; loss type and held-out status not stated.
rows.note: The text gives the fitted equation and reports approximately 1.16× computational efficiency relative to MLA under compute-optimal training. Individual losses are not reported; the listed sweep is limited in model-size and token range.
rows.check: Same as r1. This is the study's own architecture, and the fit serves an efficiency comparison with MLA, not a test of the power-law form. The 1.16× figure is an architecture comparison, not evidence on V1.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
